No major changes to the forecast through most of the week. A dry
trade-wind pattern looks to continue across the islands through
Thursday. Thursday night into Friday, however, is a different story.
A shear line is found to the northwest of the northern CNMI that is
expected to slowly approach the region. As this shear line moves
through the Marianas, it is expected to slowly weaken, but not 
before bringing increased showers and a slight chance of
thunderstorms to the islands. POPs (Probability of Precipitation) 
look to increase to as high as 40 percent Friday through Saturday 
night. Yes, increased convection is expected, however, the rainfall 
amounts will do little to alleviate the dry conditions across the 
Marianas. Therefore, it is still recommended to prepare for expected
drought conditions over the next few weeks. Conserve water where you
can.

Marine...
The trade-wind surge that brought fresh to strong trade winds to the
waters will continue to slowly subside over the next couple of days,
then increase again as a revitalized trade-wind surge develops over
the region. The Small Craft Advisory was extended through Monday
night as frequent strong gusts look to continue through then.
Although seas are expected to build due to the increasing trade swell
and a small north swell, they are expected to remain below Small
Craft Advisory levels, reaching about 9 feet. The building trade
swell will result in surf reaching 9 to 10 feet along east facing
reefs over the next several days, resulting in a high risk of rip
currents. the rip risk will reach moderate along north facing reefs
and remain low along south and east facing.

Fire weather...
The KBDI continues to slowly increase and now sits at 581, remaining
in the high category. As the week progresses, the KBDI could reach
600 within the next few days, resulting in the fire danger becoming
very high due to the moderate to fresh winds. therefore, a Fire
Weather Watch may be needed later in the week. There will be an
increased chance of showers by Friday, however, the rainfall is not
expected to be substantial and probably will not affect the dry
conditions much. 

Eastern Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) remains the primary driver of 
weather in eastern Micronesia, enhanced by a leading edge of a trade-
wind surge that will continue to bring elevated winds and swells to
the area. While most of the convection is expected to remain
concentrated south of the NET axis, proximity to Kosrae will bring
periods of patchy showers and thunderstorms to Kosrae tonight, to
then slowly taper down thereafter. In the meantime, a dry regime will
ensue at Pohnpei for much of the forecast period, meanwhile the
Near-Equatorial Trade-Wind Convergence (NETWC) will continue to build
and shift northward from the Equator, bringing on-and-off showers and
some thunderstorms to Majuro early next week.

Based on most recent scatterometer passes, the trade-wind surge has 
weakened enough to allow winds to fall below levels hazardous to 
small craft in Pohnpei coastal waters, so the Small Craft Advisory
has been allowed to expire. In addition, trade swell has diminished 
enough to allow surf to fall below hazardous criteria of 9 feet along
north facing reefs of Pohnpei and Kosrae, but surf will remain
hazardous along east facing reefs of Kosrae coming into Monday. As
such, the High Surf Advisory was allowed to expire for Pohnpei, but
will continue for Kosrae through at least Monday afternoon. Combined
seas of 6 to 8 feet in Pohnpei and Kosrae waters will slowly diminish
through midweek, to then begin increasing once again by the next
weekend as another pulse in the trade winds brings back much more
significant trade swell. In Majuro, combined seas of 7 to 9 feet will
persist through midweek to then decrease a few feet briefly, with
seas increasing significantly come next weekend, potentially
producing sea conditions hazardous to small craft.

Western Micronesia...
There are two major weather features over the region. The first is a
trough just to the west of Palau. The second is an area of trade-wind
convergence over Chuuk. With a NET remaining in the southern portion
of the region

The trough will bring high-end scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms to the islands. Rainfall totals tonight are expected to
be up to 0.5 inches. Showers are forecast to move off the islands by
Monday morning. A drying out period is anticipated for the rest of 
the week. 

The area of low pressure is producing trade-wind convergence over 
Chuuk. Model guidance suggests the system will move east, and remain 
south of Pohnpei for the next several days. This will pull the 
convergence area to the east of Chuuk and consequentially the showers
will move with it. A drying period is forecast to build in once the 
low moves eastward.
